answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure creates a false choice between unsustainable discounting and inaction. The archived data shows exp_73 acquired SMB customers via 40% discount but lost 12% at renewal—this is not a durable response. Instead, activation_messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to meaningful first action; combined with simplified onboarding (memory_86, memory_31), this compounds time-to-value and early habit formation. The goal is to lock customers into product value before price sensitivity becomes the decision variable at renewal. This approach preserves cash, targets the cohort at highest churn risk (price-sensitive SMB), and builds on proven levers. Referral incentives work well for *established* customers (memory_57), not for at-risk new SMB. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the current SMB churn crisis. A standard experiment on activation messaging + streamlined onboarding in the at-risk SMB segment tests whether stronger early engagement reduces price-driven churn without committing margin. The uncertainty is whether activation messaging alone can overcome deep price positioning; we run it at standard scale to measure before scaling further.
